script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for March 28. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Three pounds of tissue.  86 billion neurons.  100 trillion connections.

86 billion neurons, each connected to an average of 7,000 others. That's about 600 trillion synaptic connections—more than the number of stars in the Milky Way. The complexity inside your head exceeds the complexity of the galaxy. Your brain is 2% of your body weight but uses 20% of your energy.  Thinking is metabolically expensive.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: The most complex object we know of is the one doing the knowing.  Your brain is so complex that it can't fully understand itself.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Brain Wonder - Appreciate Your Complexity.

Here's your activity: Right now, your brain is interpreting symbols, understanding language, and being aware that it's doing so. Spend a moment in genuine wonder at this. The universe became complex enough to observe itself—through you. This helps you develop awe for the complexity that enables experience.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about what your brain does can be applied to brain wonder - appreciate your complexity. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
